entries.sanskrit: सप्तमे संशय-च्छेदि प्रतिनन्द्य मुनेर् वचः । पुनः क्षत्त्रा कृता नाना प्रश्नाः सम्यग् उदीरिताः ॥ अथ ते भगवल्-लीला योग-मायोपबृंहिताः\[भा।पु। ३.५.२२\] इत्य्-आदिना माया-गुणैर् लीलया भगवान् सृष्ट्य्-आदि करोतीत्य् एवं ब्रुवाणं मैत्रेयं भारत्या प्रार्थना-रूपया प्रीणयन्न् इवेत्य् अभिप्रायाज्ञानेनाक्षेपात् ॥१॥

In the seventh chapter, after honoring the sage’s words that cut doubt, Vidura again properly voiced many questions. When Maitreya had said that the Lord performs creation and the rest through māyā’s qualities as play, Vidura, as though pleasing him with a prayer, challenged the implication that this meaning is already understood.

entries.sanskrit: अर्भकवल् लीलापि न युज्यते वैषम्याद् इत्य् आह---उद्यमयति प्रवर्तयतीत्य् उद्यमः। अर्भकस्य क्रीडायां प्रवृत्ति-हेतुः कामोऽस्ति । अन्यतस् तु वस्त्व्-अन्तरेण बालान्तर-प्रवर्तनेन वा तस्य क्रीडेच्छा भवति । ईश्वरस्य तु स्वतस् तृप्तस्य कथं कामः ? अन्यतः सदा निवृत्तस्य चासङ्गाद् अद्वितीयस्य कथम् अन्यतश् चिक्रीडिषा ? इत्य् अर्थः ॥३॥

Even play like a child’s appears unsuitable because it would imply partiality. “Effort” means causing activity. A child plays from desire; desire may also arise from another object or from another child’s activity. But the Lord is satisfied in Himself—how could He have desire? Since He is always withdrawn from anything other than Himself, unattached and nondual, how could He wish to play with another?

Vidura repeats the earlier statement in order to challenge it: the Lord creates for the enjoyment of the living being who is deluded by the guṇamayī māyā. That māyā produces the jīva’s delusion of being the doer and enjoyer; through it the Lord created. The cited teaching says that the deluded jīva mistakes himself for a three-guṇa being and accepts the resulting harm as his own. Here “establishes” means “protects,” while “will withdraw” means that He will make the obscuring power disappear in reverse order; another reading means that He will hold it completely within Himself.

entries.sanskrit: एतच् च जीवस्याविद्याश्रयत्वे घटेत, न तु तत् संभवतीत्य् आह---देशत इति । योऽसौ देशादिभिर् अविलुप्तावबोध आत्मा जीवः, ब्रह्म-स्वरूपत्वात् । स कथम् अजयाऽविद्यया युज्येत? तत्र देशतो दीप-प्रभाया इव लोपो नास्ति, सर्व-गतत्वात् । न कालतः, विद्युत इव नित्यत्वात् । नावस्थातः, स्मृतिवद् अविक्रियत्वात् । न स्वतः, स्वप्नवत् सत्यत्वात् । नान्यतः, घटादिवद् अद्वितीयत्वात् । एवम् एतैर् यस्य बोधो न लुप्यते, स कथम् अजया युज्येत ? अजा चात्राविद्यैव, न माया, तस्या अवबोधेन विरोधाभावात् ॥५॥

This explanation could apply if the jīva were truly the seat of ignorance, but that cannot be so. The self, whose awareness is not diminished by place or anything else, is the jīva because it has Brahman’s nature. How could it be joined to beginningless ignorance? There is no loss through place, because awareness is all-pervading like a lamp’s radiance; no loss through time, because it is eternal like lightning; no loss through condition, because it is unchanging like memory; no loss through itself, because it is real like a dream; and no loss through another, because it is nondual like a pot. Since the awareness of such a self is never lost, how could it be joined to beginningless ignorance? Here “the beginningless one” means ignorance, not the Lord’s māyā, because awareness does not conflict with māyā itself.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, ब्रह्म-रूपत्वाद् एव जीवस्य संसारोऽपि न विद्यत इत्य् आक्षिपति । सर्व-क्षेत्रेष्व् अवस्थितो भोक्तापि वस्तुतो भगवान् एव, चिद्-रूपत्वेन तद्-व्यतिरेकाभावात् । एवं च सत्य् अमुष्य जीवस्य दुर्भगत्वम् आनन्दादि-भ्रंशः कर्मभिर् हेतु-भूतैः क्लेशो वा कुतः? कर्म-संबन्धाभावात् । अन्यथेश्वरस्यापि तत्-प्रसङ्गः स्याद् इति भावः ॥६॥

Moreover, because the jīva has Brahman’s nature, saṃsāra does not truly exist for it. Although the enjoyer present in every field, the Lord alone exists in reality, because consciousness has no difference from Him. Then how could this jīva become unfortunate, lose bliss and the like, or suffer through karma? There is no connection with karma; otherwise the same consequence would fall upon the Lord.

प्रतीयेत\[भा।पु। २.९.३३\] इत्य् आदौ मायाया आभास-स्थानीयत्वं प्रदर्श्य, तद्-अस्पृश्यत्वम् एव भगवतो दर्शितम् । त्वम् आद्यः पुरुषः साक्षाद् \[भा।पु। १.७.२३\] इत्य् आदौ, माया व्युदस्य चिच्-छक्त्या इत्य् अनेन च तथा ज्ञापितम् । माया परैत्याभिमुखे च विलज्जामाना\[भा।पु। २.७.४७\] इत्य् अनेन च । [^२४]: प्राधान्यम् इति क्वचित् पाठः। तद् एवं भगवति तद्-विरोधं परिहृत्य जीवेऽप्य् अविद्या-सम्बन्धम् अतर्क्यत्वेन दर्शिततया तन् माययैव समादधाति । ईश्वरस्य इति यद् इत्य् अनेनैव सम्बध्यते । अर्थ-वशाद् अत्र च तृतीयया परिणम्यते । यत् यथा ईश्वरस्य स्वरूप-ज्ञानादिभिः समर्थस्य, अत एव विमुक्तस्य \[जीवस्य[^२५]\] कार्पण्यं तत्-तत्-प्रकाश-तिरोभावः, तथा बन्धनं दर्शित-गुण-मय-जाल-प्रवेशश् च भवतीति । तद् उक्तं---तत्-सङ्ग-भ्रंशितैश्वर्यं \[भा।पु। ६.५.१५\] इति । [^२५]: परमात्म-सन्दर्भस्य पाठः। तद् एवं सर्वम् अभिप्रेत्य श्रुतयोऽप्य् आहुः---स यद् अजया त्व् अजां \[भा।पु। १०.८७.३८\] इत्य्-आदाव् अपेत-भग इति च । अत्र मूल-पद्ये भगवतो मायेत्य् अनेन भगवत्त्वं मायिकम्[^२६] इत्य् आयातम् । इन्द्रस्य मायेत्य् अत्र यथेन्द्रत्वम् एवं पूर्वत्रापि ज्ञेयम् ॥९॥ \[परमात्म-सन्दर्भ २५, ९०\] [^२६]: \"भगवत्त्वं त्व् अमायिकं\" इति, \"भगवत्-तत्त्वम् अमायिकं\" इति च द्वौ पाठौ परमात्म-सन्दर्भे ड्र्श्येते।

Since mere consciousness alone cannot explain the jīva either, Maitreya accepts the jīva’s divine status and says “this.” The power by which cosmic creation and the rest occur is the Lord’s inconceivable self-power called māyā. Because it is beyond reasoning, it is itself inconceivable. Although both the Lord and His māyā are inconceivable, the phrase “the Lord’s māyā” shows that māyā is His external power, whereas the Lord’s own power is internal; therefore the external guṇas and their effects—maintenance and the rest—do not touch Him. The cited Tantric explanation means that whatever is not opposed to the Lord through māyā is not made an object of contradiction; and what is not opposed to Him is not thereby made wholly nonexistent. The examples from the Purāṇa establish that the Lord creates, maintains and destroys with qualities while remaining without limiting qualities, because His inconceivable power accomplishes both sides. The same reasoning removes the charge of partiality: the Lord’s self-power is primary, while māyā appears as an external reflection. The note then explains that the jīva’s bondage, poverty and obscuration of knowledge are also arranged through that same inconceivable māyā. Thus the Lord’s divine status is not produced by māyā; rather, His māyā belongs to one who is already Bhagavān, while the jīva’s limitation is the concealment of powers that are otherwise present.

entries.sanskrit: उत्तरम् अभिनन्दन्न् आत्मनः कृतार्थताम् आविष्करोति---सञ्छिन्न इति षड्भिः । चिद्-रूपत्वाविशेषेऽपि कथम् ईश्वरस्य जगत्-कर्तृत्वादि, कथं वा जीवस्य संसारः ? इति यः संशयो ममासीत्, स तव सूक्तं सोपपत्तिकं वाक्यम् एवासिः खड्गस् तेन सञ्छिन्नः । अत इदानीं मे मन उभयत्रापीश्वर-स्वातन्त्र्ये जीव-पारतन्त्र्ये च सम्प्रधावति सम्यक् प्रविशति । एवं वाविलुप्तावबोध-रूपस्यात्मनः कथम् अविद्यया बन्धः, कुतो वा तन्-निवृत्तिः ? इति संशयः । उभयत्रेति, बन्धे मोक्षे चेत्य् अर्थः ॥१५॥

The remaining doubt was how the self, whose awareness is not lost, can be bound by ignorance and how that bondage can end; “both” means bondage and liberation.

He says that my doubt arose from limited knowledge. The person sunk in the deepest delusion and attached to the body, and the person who has reached the Lord beyond material intelligence, live and flourish according to their respective condition, because they are free from the torment of doubt. But one who wants to abandon the world by dwelling on suffering cannot remain steady, because he lacks direct experience of his own bliss; therefore he suffers.

That too will cease through your favor. “The nonself has no reality” means that the perceived world has no independent substance; it has only the status of an appearance. By service at your feet and by firm understanding I shall remove even that appearance.

The five beginning with prāṇa and the five beginning with Nāga make ten kinds. The senses and their objects are also included. The repeated mention of “objects and senses” identifies their presiding deities, together with them. Because prāṇa supports everything, the senses and their deities are said to accompany it. Thus the prāṇa described by you is threefold through the three divisions; its manifestations, beginning with Brahmā, are denoted by the word creation.

The seventh chapter has again stated the many questions of Vidura, after he honored the sage’s words that cut doubt. The passage about the Lord’s play, supported by yoga-māyā, provoked the challenge. “One who is questioned about the Purāṇa” means one whose understanding of the Purāṇa has been sought; thus this foremost sage, delighted by the narration of Bhagavān, was encouraged and smiled.
